Lead comprehensive codebase and database inventories using static analysis tooling, quantifying code composition, identifying architectural patterns and anti-patterns, and distinguishing auto-generated code from hand-written business logic

12+ years of software architecture and engineering experience
Deep expertise in .NET Framework: must be able to read, understand, and assess Web Forms (code-behind, ViewState, page lifecycle), MVC (controllers, Razor views), and legacy patterns common in 15-20 year old applications
Backend/API design experience: RESTful API design, authentication/authorization patterns (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT), session-to-token migration strategies
Experience with legacy application modernization: experience migrating server-rendered .NET applications to modern SPA frameworks
Experience with static code analysis tools (SonarQube, NDepend, or equivalents)
Strong architectural documentation skills: ability to produce clear architecture diagrams (C4 model preferred), complexity heat maps, and technical assessment reports
Experience with migration patterns and when to apply them: strangler fig, micro-frontends, API gateway patterns, parallel running strategies
Demonstratable hands-on experience with AI-assisted development tools

Experience with TypeScript
Ability to reverse-engineer undocumented systems: extract architecture, patterns, and business rules from code in the absence of documentation
Experience with reporting migration (SSRS, Crystal Reports)
Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools for code analysis and documentation
Experience with third-party .NET UI controls (Telerik, DevExpress, Infragistics) and their React equivalents
Cloud architecture experience
Experience with SignalR/WebSocket migration to React real-time patterns
Performance engineering experience: ability to identify and plan for performance-critical migration areas
Experience in React must be able to design a production-grade React architecture including state management, component design patterns, routing, build tooling, and API integration patterns

jobs.description:
Senior Azure Platform Engineer | Eindhoven | €120k OTE + Indefinite Contract | Build a self-service Azure platform for mission-critical workloads at one of the top 100 companies in the Netherlands | Azure, Python/GO, GitOps, Helm, CI/CD

How do you feel about working on the core, most vital infrastructure, that runs the most mission critical workloads in The Netherlands?

Our client is a mission-critical MSP that helps around 40 enterprise clients in the Netherlands design infrastructure that's air-gapped and runs their most critical workloads. This is done through self-steering teams and close cooperation, using the latest best practices to ensure strict requirements are met. If the platform goes down, vital parts of Dutch society go down — think energy supply, payment and ATM infrastructure, edge devices, fraud detection, and anti-money-laundering systems. The core focus is the complete (re)design of cloud and cloud-native solutions, and migrations from old, legacy environments to new cloud-native infrastructure.
Beyond building cloud-native Azure solutions, the organization is also keen on open-source, private cloud. It's about 500 FTE, 75% of whom are engineers. Overall, you'll have the chance to make a real impact.

Your role:

As an Azure Platform Engineer, you'll start by working on a highly complex refactor of a 30-year-old ERP system. In this role, you'll be responsible for the CI/CD architecture, designing Azure infrastructure, and automating all the processes. A software engineering background is preferred, as you won't be responsible for the core infrastructure itself, but mainly for building self-service functionality within Azure. You'll also advise the infrastructure team on (software) architecture matters, Platform Engineering best practices, and how to use IaC to roll out mostly Azure-native resources. You'll work on this project together with your team and the client. The application itself is a .NET application containing a lot of complex business logic — it's extremely mission-critical, and downtime would be severe. You'll ensure SLO/SLA requirements are met and design watertight solutions with 99.9%+ availability. The complete tech stack is yet to be defined.

Your profile:

5+ years in Software engineering, several of them on Azure at scale
You've designed and built cloud platforms at more than one organization
Experience with multi-region and global setups, connectivity, identity, and security boundaries
Terraform or Bicep as your default, plus Bash/PowerShell or Python
A background prior to cloud — for example, data center, bare metal, or virtualization
Comfortable leading technical discussions with a client's engineers and architects
Fluent in English; Dutch is a plus

How do you feel about working on the core, most vital infrastructure, that runs the most mission critical workloads in The Netherlands?

Our client is a mission-critical MSP that helps around 40 enterprise clients in the Netherlands design infrastructure that's air-gapped and runs their most critical workloads. If the platform goes down, vital parts of Dutch society go down — think energy supply, payment and ATM infrastructure, edge devices, fraud detection, and anti-money-laundering systems. The core focus is the complete (re)design of cloud and cloud-native solutions, and migrations from old, legacy environments to new cloud-native infrastructure.

In this role, you'll be responsible for the CI/CD architecture, designing Azure infrastructure, and automating all the processes. A software engineering background is preferred, as you won't be responsible for the core infrastructure itself, but mainly for building self-service functionality within Azure. You'll also advise the infrastructure team on (software) architecture matters, Platform Engineering best practices, and how to use IaC to roll out mostly Azure-native resources. You'll work on this project together with your team and the client. The application itself is a .NET application containing a lot of complex business logic — it's extremely mission-critical, and downtime would be severe.
